BERT4Rec predicts an appended reserved MASK, consistent with its [masked-item objective](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690). Adapter implication: truncate history to L−1, append MASK, then left-pad to L; `F = log2feats(sequence)` is B×L×D and the query is `F[:, -1, :]`, never `F[:, count_nonzero-1, :]`. For variable MASK positions `p`, gather `F[torch.arange(B, device=F.device), p]`. Position-wise candidates B×L must be gathered with the same batch/position indices. For K candidates per query, pair features B×1×D with candidate embeddings B×K×D; elementwise multiplication followed by sum over D yields B×K. If `predict_score` requires aligned positions, expand queries to B×K×D explicitly. Preserve the trained scoring head, including transformations/biases, and use evaluation mode without gradients.

For diagnostic text retrieval, keep catalog rows in fixed item-ID order; fit one [TfidfVectorizer](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.feature_extraction.text.TfidfVectorizer.html) on permitted titles/descriptions and transform targets with that same vocabulary. L2-normalized TF-IDF makes dot products equal cosine similarity. Compute target-row or small target-batch against catalog using [cosine_similarity(Q, X, dense_output=False)](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.metrics.pairwise.cosine_similarity.html), with both inputs sparse; never construct catalog-by-catalog similarities. Empty/tokenless text produces zero rows when a vocabulary exists; an entirely tokenless fitting corpus requires an explicit empty-vocabulary fallback.

Recommended deterministic policy: retain strictly positive similarities, exclude self/other ineligible IDs, then order by descending score and ascending item ID using [np.lexsort((item_ids, -scores))](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/generated/numpy.lexsort.html). Return fewer than k when necessary; zero similarity means no textual evidence. If exactly k is required, explicitly fill with eligible zero-score IDs in ascending order. Avoid arbitrary partition-boundary ties. Keep this retrieval diagnostic-only; the deployed predictor remains the single trained BERT4Rec.
